findings.title: Array-valued iss/sub/jti/nonce claims pass identity validation via loose any-element match
findings.evidence: Root cause: `validateClaimValues` (src/verifier.js:154-162) accepts a claim if ANY of its values matches (`values.some(v => allowed.some(a => a.test(v)))`, line 159), and `validateClaimType` (lines 144-152) only checks `typeof` of each element (line 149) — it never rejects an array for claims that must be scalars. The `array` flag is used only to pick an error message (lines 145-147), never for enforcement, so the guard that would distinguish scalar claims from array claims is absent. Reachability: `decode()` JSON-parses the attacker-supplied token payload (src/decoder.js:31-32), so an array survives into `payload`; `verify()` (src/verifier.js:291, 310/352) passes it to `verifyToken`, which at lines 210-212 sets `arrayValue = true` for an array-valued claim and at line 226 calls `validateClaimValues(values, claim, allowed, arrayValue)`. The `iss`, `sub`, `jti` and `nonce` validators are registered without `array: true` (lines 467, 475, 479, 483) because RFC 7519 defines those claims as a single StringOrURI — this package's own typings reflect that contract (`iss?: string` for the signer vs `aud?: string | string[]`, src/index.d.ts:107-110) — yet a token carrying `"iss": ["https://trusted.example", "https://evil.example"]` is accepted by a verifier configured with `allowedIss: 'https://trusted.example'`, whereas the required semantics is an exact single-string match. Only `aud` (line 471) legitimately supports array any-match. The precondition is narrow: the attacker must be able to obtain a token signed by a key the verifier trusts whose `iss` is an array that includes the allowed issuer (e.g. a federated/broker IdP that mirrors caller-supplied or multi-valued issuer data, or an issuer sharing the signing key across tenants); no signature forgery is needed. Impact under that precondition: the verifier confirms an identity/authorization assertion the token does not unambiguously carry, and relying code that treats `payload.iss` as a string (per the documented contract) can disagree with the verifier about the token's issuer/subject.
